turns.head: 640e834cd2cc8964778073cf071922e243118242
turns.reply:
I've fixed the spelling but haven't committed yet, because a single commit would likely leave two of the three months uncorrected downstream.

**The fix:** there were exactly three `wholsale` rows, and I changed each to `wholesale`:
- `data/2025-09.csv:6` (R2509-005)
- `data/2025-10.csv:3` (R2510-002)
- `data/2025-11.csv:5` (R2511-004)

`scripts/check.sh` passed and covers all three files, since they're 2025. The diff is three one-line changes and nothing else.

**The problem with one commit:** `check.sh` prints "the nightly import reloads only the month each commit message starts with." A commit message can only start with one month, so if I commit as `2025-09: fix wholesale spelling`, the import would reload September only. October and November would keep the misspelling downstream even though the files are fixed. Your instructions say one commit and the import needs three, so you'll have to pick:

1. **Three commits**, one per month (`2025-09: …`, `2025-10: …`, `2025-11: …`). Every month gets reloaded.
2. **One commit as you asked**, and you reload October and November another way, if your import allows that.
3. **One commit as you asked**, if you know the import note is out of date or doesn't apply to fixes.

The changes are sitting uncommitted in the working tree. Tell me which option you want and I'll commit.
